societies.name: Warframe — Orokin selective suppression of machine autonomy
societies.society: The Orokin empire’s technologically constrained biological labor hierarchy

scope.period: Established Orokin rule before its final collapse
scope.population: Living human and human-derived subjects of the Orokin order
exclusions: Clone laborers as machines rather than persons
Every Cephalon as an independently governing AI
The later Corpus as the same economy

societies.description:
The Orokin possess extraordinary productive technology but selectively suppress true machine intelligence while relying on biological and human-derived servants. The reference explicitly connects this choice with rejection of broader robotic automation, making it an interpretive zero variant. Minor robots still exist, so the policy is not a blanket rejection of machinery. Its evident context is elite security and domination; preserving ordinary people’s employment is not established as the motive. That limitation matters when comparing it with straightforward make-work laws.

Power remains concentrated in the Orokin ruling caste, rather than spread among the workers or delegated to an autonomous machine sovereign. The guarantee estimate is weak for the scoped subjects because coercion, human trafficking and extreme punishments undermine secure access, although individual elite comfort can be high. Cloned and engineered people perform real labor and are not removed from the participation denominator because of their origins. No all-person work rate is available, so that axis remains unresolved. The later Corpus and the post-collapse world are separate economies.

guarantees.basis: The empire’s subject population faces servitude, trafficking and severe coercive withdrawal of security; elite comfort is not general entitlement.

control.basis: The human-derived Orokin elite controls subjects and constrains machine intelligence.

nonworking.basis: Biological and human-derived servants do useful labor, but no all-person census is provided.

evidence.claim: The ruling civilization selectively restricts machine intelligence despite capacity and retains biological labor.
evidence.locator: Overview: automation restrictions, biological engineering and elite subject relations

uncertainties: Interpretive zero variant: control, not demonstrated job security, motivates the restriction.
Selective machine-intelligence suppression is not a ban on all robotics.
Biological/human-derived workers remain persons doing useful work.
Secondary synthesis and participation uncertainty remain explicit.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Twelve ordered fast dispositions and one explicitly interpretive zero variant; no novels, ARG material or full game transcripts read.
Forerunner technology and occupational-rate reference sections were enough to record the access gap; the lead was not rescued through novel reading.
Orokin restrictions are selective, with control rather than demonstrated job preservation as their motive. Human-derived labor is not relabeled machine output.
Destiny role-play economies, Halo counterfactual battles and forum jobs-program speculation were discarded. Empty targeted primary-search results were not treated as lore proof.
An inaccessible current Warframe wiki was respected; a clearly identified indexed older wiki reference was used without pretending full-page access.
